question.text: What is the role of KRA (KYC Registration Agency) in the mutual fund KYC ecosystem?

answer.text: KRA issues PAN cards to investors who don't have one

KRA maintains KYC information, enables inter-operability among SEBI-registered intermediaries, and may share information with other market regulators such as RBI, IRDAI, and PFRDA if the respective regulators notify so
KRA only stores PAN data and verifies it with the IT Department
KRA directly processes mutual fund transactions for KYC-compliant investors

explanation.text: The Logic: KRAs maintain KYC information and enable interoperability among SEBI-registered intermediaries, so an investor who completes KYC once need not repeat it with another SEBI intermediary. KRAs may also share KYC information with other market regulators — such as RBI, IRDAI, and PFRDA — if the respective regulators notify so. The Trap: KRAs do not process mutual fund transactions and do not issue PAN cards. Cross-regulator sharing is gated on the other regulator's notification — it is not automatic sharing with every regulated entity. Note: Before initiating a fresh KYC, check the investor's KYC status on the KRA system; if KYC is already validated, the existing record can be relied upon as per applicable norms.
